## What stays, adapts and may look different

“Stays” describes intended product behavior and ownership, not a claim that
every current source file can remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

| Area | Can stay as the user experiences it | Internal adaptation or visible difference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Portal shell | Layout, navigation, session URLs, workspace selection, host authentication and file links | Keep existing host/Go application; replace runtime composition. No p2 adoption. |
| Repository and operations features | Compare/review, worktrees, Files, clusters, reservations and existing lifecycle controls | Reconnect agent status/notifications; preserve domain authority and recovery journals. |
| Chat | Composer, streamed transcript, uploads, history paging, stop, queue and model controls | Generalize conversation client/types and translate Pi events/history. Existing DOM/styles can remain; Codex item shapes and transport cannot. |
| Providers | Existing workspace default and session selector, model validation, progress and error handling | Native Pi model/provider change replaces native-thread closing/reopening. Auth/catalog discovery and token resolution change. A provider may offer different thinking levels or models. |
| Teams | Addresses, retained members, assignments, reviewers, separate transcripts and report-to-lead workflow | Preserve portal roster/orchestration. Replace thread creation, activity, dispatch, utility launches and native caller binding with backend equivalents. |
| Planning | Existing Plan/Default and implement-plan workflow can be retained | Custom mode/transition handling and accepted-plan identity are required. Do not mistake the upstream example for a complete enforcement boundary. |
| Existing sessions | Codex sessions remain editable, runnable and recoverable, including their members and tools | Retain the supported Codex backend and state. A Pi continuation is a new derived conversation, not a lossless conversion or retirement of the original. |
| Optional questions | Show choices/free text while the agent keeps working; accept a later answer in the correct conversation | Add durable question and answer identities with host-owned delivery; do not substitute a blocking Pi dialog. |
| Session resources | Existing portal remains the place to inspect and control a session | New session-owned cgroup/namespace, mounted temporary storage and per-session resource display; retain existing authorization and recovery. |
| Quotas/account UI | Existing private-pool usage preview can remain host-owned | Pi token/cost usage is not Codex subscription allowance/reset parity. Unsupported account operations need an honest unavailable state or a separately verified adapter. |
| Terminal | Existing Codex sessions can keep their established terminal path during coexistence | Pi's native TUI is not automatically an attach client for a portal-owned SDK session. Shared live web/CLI access is separate optional work. |

The present provider selection applies to the whole development session,
including retained members. The user now requests an additional hierarchy:
session default, explicit member override, and explicit provider/model fallback
chain. Retain the existing default behavior for members without an override.
All members still belong to the same development-session process boundary,
even when they use different providers. Backend choice (Codex or Pi) and model
provider choice are separate; switching a Pi member's provider is not a
cross-backend migration.

Model responses, compaction wording and tool presentation cannot be promised
identical. Pi retains text/tool history across providers, but drops another
model's reasoning when constructing its context. Thinking is adjusted to the
selected model's supported levels. Preserve original history for display;
distinguish it from what the next model actually receives.

## Backend choice and architectural boundary

codex-web already separates trusted application conversation IDs from native
clients through `conversation.Client` and `Target`, but method signatures use
`codex.*` types. Generalizing that narrow seam is plausible. The scope is the
operations needed by the portal, not an emulation server for arbitrary Codex
clients. Keep generic UI behavior and application authority outside the backend.

The smallest useful portal capability contract is the following. Keep its
implementation in the existing portal and a session worker adapter; do not
build a new general-purpose agent server.

| Capability | Minimum contract |
| --- | --- |
| Identity and lifecycle | Backend-tagged trusted session/member/conversation identity, incarnation and package generation; create/load/fork/interrupt/recover through existing authority. Old schema-1 authority rejects unknown fields, so version routing deliberately. |
| Conversation view | Paged history, typed text/tool/question projections, live updates and reconnect cursor; preserve raw backend evidence separately. A view projection is not an execution-state migration. |
| Admission and execution | Stable immutable input/queue IDs, acceptance receipt or honest unknown state, steering/follow-up semantics, cancellation and terminal/settled observations. |
| Settings and routing | Session defaults, member override, exact provider/model/thinking and fallback policy; capture effective settings on admission and actual provider on execution. |
| Host interaction | Caller-bound reporting, utility/peer delivery and persistent optional questions/answers; existing authorization, origin checks and held-recipient rules. |
| Ownership and accounting | Session supervisor/cgroup/namespace identity, owned tool/service handles, mounted temporary paths, resource observations and recovery holds. |

Backend, conversation and provider identities are distinct. Only trusted host
state selects paths, endpoints and member identities. Unsupported capabilities
must be explicit; never silently downgrade editable Codex sessions to viewers.

| Candidate | Evidence and benefit | Cost or decisive limit | Position |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Coding-agent SDK in per-session worker processes | Direct sessions, tools, resource loaders, credentials and extension hooks; retains standard coding-agent features | Adds pinned worker packaging and a narrow host transport; durable admission is not supplied by `prompt()` | Candidate alongside RPC, subject to receipt/recovery gate |
| `pi --mode rpc` subprocess | Native JSONL commands/events; natural Go process boundary; custom tools can be loaded as extensions | Correlation IDs are not deduplication; custom tools/auth need extension or extra control path; UI supports dialogs but not arbitrary TUI widgets | Viable simpler comparator, not rejected merely for using RPC |
| Pi Durable service | Atomic admissions, `requestId` dedup, persisted tasks, child/report recovery, safe/unsafe replay declarations | Explicitly experimental; separate data format and resource/tool integration; single-writer ownership and upgrade policy required | Compare if supported SDK cannot meet recovery without a fork |
| pi-ai / agent-core directly | Provider and agent-loop components with maximum host control | We own substantially more harness, history, tool and recovery behavior | Higher-cost fallback, not the default |
| p2 / wholesale Chord application | Demonstrates browser/TUI and durable-agent integration | p2 explicitly says unsupported prototype, will disappear, do not build on it; replaces a portal the user likes | Reject for this task |

RPC is not excluded by web dialogs: `select`, `confirm`, `input` and `editor`
are supported. The SDK advantage is explicit ownership of tools, resources,
policy and callbacks, not an unsupported claim that RPC cannot host custom
tools. Runtime services should have one authoritative writer per conversation
and reconnecting clients; browsers do not spawn independent file writers.

### One session process tree, namespace and temporary storage

The intended topology is portal → session supervisor → lead/member workers →
tools and registered temporary services. The supervisor enters one owned cgroup
and mount namespace before spawning any worker. Every member/provider uses that
same session boundary. Workers may be unloaded only after queues, uncertain
submissions, active tools, utilities and terminal subscriptions permit it under
existing recovery rules; unloading is not archiving or deleting a session.

[Process/isolation evidence](process-isolation-evidence.md) establishes two
concrete integration obligations. The current session-service helper launches
sibling `app.slice` units, so its spawn path must enter the session supervisor
while preserving registration and shutdown/recovery contracts. `JoinsNamespaceOf`
shares temporary directories, not the exact mount namespace; mounts created by
`ExecStartPre` do not establish the later worker namespace. Use one owning
`ExecStart` process and inherited descendants rather than claim that sibling
units automatically provide the requested boundary.

Give each session explicit backing directories mounted at its temporary paths,
with persistent ownership metadata outside those temporary mounts: session
incarnation, supervisor generation, cgroup, namespace identity, backing paths
and live command/service leases. Keep recovery records and receipts on durable
storage, not ephemeral tmpfs. Recreating the worker must preserve temporary
paths that accepted work still depends on. Namespace exit removes its view;
it does not authorize deleting backing data. Retain the ordinary explicit
lifecycle/cleanup authorization and interrupted-operation recovery rules.
Prefer disk-backed scratch for the first comparison; stock `PrivateTmp` and
`RuntimeDirectory` stop-time cleanup must not erase retained recovery inputs.
Directory allocated-block telemetry is observed usage, not a hard allocation
budget: deleted-but-open files can be missed, and `df` on a bind mount still
reports the shared filesystem. Quotas, dedicated filesystems or bounded tmpfs
need separate capacity/permission choices; no hard storage limit is assumed.

Rootless systemd mount isolation is not yet proved with the required tool
permissions. `PrivateUsers` can change host-root/setuid/sudo behavior; a narrow
host-managed launcher that establishes mounts then runs as the original UID is
an alternative to validate, not an approved deployment. Do not grant mount
administration privileges to agents. This is a bounded host-permission decision,
not a project to defend against the already trusted local operator.

Account the session's CPU, memory/peak, process count and I/O from its cgroup,
and temporary-storage usage from its owned backing paths. Label cache versus
anonymous memory and excluded/shared services. Nix daemon builders and existing
shared tmux are not inherited worker descendants; do not charge their whole
resource use to one session or assert complete attribution. The existing shared
Codex daemon remains an explicit transitional limitation for legacy sessions.
Retroactively rehosting it is outside this package; side-by-side support does
not pretend that legacy execution already has the new Pi isolation boundary.

## Hard contracts and release gates

### Providers, credentials and model catalogs

[`AgentSession.setModel()`][setmodel] validates auth, changes the existing
agent's model, appends a model-change entry and adjusts thinking. This directly
addresses the provider-switch motivation. Custom compatible endpoints are
supported; the existing private Responses gateway still needs an exact check.
Initially perform managed changes at a settled boundary, preserving retained
member identities, queue order and instructions. Mapping interrupted switches
to the current journal/continuation semantics is part of acceptance, not a reason
to discard those guarantees.

Source exposes OpenAI API keys and ChatGPT OAuth, separate `openai-codex` OAuth,
Anthropic API/subscription auth, Copilot and other provider adapters. These are
available mechanisms, not proof of the user's account entitlements or exact
model access. Credentials remain server-side. Preserve trusted private endpoint
and token-file configuration; do not accept executable paths or secrets from
ordinary model-selection input. Unknown quota data remains unknown.

Pin a coherent Pi/Node/dependency set and explicitly control model catalog
updates: Pi can overlay pi.dev catalog data at runtime, so a source pin alone
does not freeze the model choices. Preserve portal catalog validation and
record supported provider/model/thinking combinations. Credential refresh,
custom endpoint compatibility and unsupported-model errors are release gates.

The new override/fallback policy is session default → optional member override
→ an explicit ordered provider/account/model chain. An override affects only
that member, never a global endpoint or another member's settings. Preserve
the requested and effective thinking level and the actual physical provider on
each attempt. For the user's example, “Snajpa codex-lb → subscription Daybreak”
is a requested binding/route; Daybreak's canonical model ID and subscription
availability have not been verified. Do not offer it through an API-key pool
merely because a similarly named model appears in a catalog.

Pi has a supported virtual-model `route()` hook that receives the previous
physical model, failed response and persisted branch state. This can select a
different provider on a retry. However, the coding-agent only initiates that
retry when its own error classifier and budget admit it. A custom router alone
does not make every cybersec/content error retryable. Model text refusals are
ordinary text, not a structured provider failure. The
[fallback evidence](provider-fallback-evidence.md) pins the exact routing,
retry-gate and response-normalization sources.

Implement an explicit, finite host policy for verified error categories; use
native routing where its admission semantics fit and a supported host
continuation only where separately proved. Preserve unclassified outcomes and
do not infer a security-error category from arbitrary assistant prose. Record
policy revision, chain position, original input/switch identity, observed error,
old/new provider/account/model and prepared/applied/verified/unknown status.
Keep the active provider and reason visible. Bound the combined provider
retries, agent retries and fallback hops so separate retry loops do not multiply
uncontrolled work. Never replay a tool or accepted prompt just because the
fallback provider lacks part of the preceding response.

### Authentication ownership across workers and legacy Codex

**Use native Pi shared storage first; do not build a broker solely for worker
count.** The pinned source supports independent processes sharing one canonical
writable `AuthStorage` file and provider credential key. It acquires a
cross-process lock before rereading stored JSON, rechecks expiry under that
lock, holds the lock through OAuth refresh, and writes the rotated credentials
before release. One authoritative entry/refresh coordinator can therefore serve
all workers using that account/grant. Separate session processes do not imply
interactive login per worker. This is supported source behavior, not a live concurrency
test of this deployment; [authentication evidence](authentication-evidence.md)
records the exact implementation and limits.
The lock is not an atomic transaction with OpenAI: a lost refresh response,
failed credential write or abrupt worker death after token rotation can still
require reauthentication. Do not promise automatic repair on HTTP 401; the
inspected normal refresh path is expiry-based. Custom/in-memory/read-only stores
do not inherit the canonical writable file backend's coordination behavior.

Per-session mount namespaces must expose the **same underlying credential
directory, authoritative data and lock sidecars**, with rotation/replacement
visible to every participant. Do not copy `auth.json` into session scratch or
bind only a file into separate directories whose adjacent lock files differ.
This narrow shared control-plane data is compatible with separate agent process
trees. It must survive worker restarts and session scratch cleanup.

Pi auth entries are keyed by provider ID, not member or UI account alias. Use one
account-bound credential reference for workers sharing the same grant; do not
clone it into independently refreshed aliases. Distinct accounts need explicit
store/key mapping. Pi's ordinary Codex OAuth client and its ChatGPT direct-token
flow are different client/scope/transport contracts, not interchangeable labels.

The existing native Codex backend has different storage and locking. Pi's lock
does not coordinate a native Codex writer. Preserve legacy authentication under
its existing owner; use separately supported independently issued grants, or an
explicit common refresh authority/compatible inference path. Do not import or
copy its current rotating grant into Pi and claim co-safe refresh. One initial
Pi login for its worker group is different from sharing legacy Codex's exact
grant. Verify that a separate grant's issuance and renewal leave legacy Codex
usable; this has not been tested. The side-by-side recommendation does not
silently change native auth.

| Choice | What it buys | Obligation / recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical native Pi store | One login and coordinated refresh among participating Pi workers, with no new service | Simplest default for trusted same-user workers; verify shared directory/lock visibility and exact account/client access. Workers can access credentials under the existing trust model. |
| Credential broker | One refresh owner keeps the refresh token central and supplies access credentials | Workers still own provider protocol, scopes and Daybreak behavior. Adds service/lease/error handling; use only for a concrete credential-access or cross-client requirement. |
| Personal inference gateway / codex-lb | One upstream auth owner and inference route; workers need no upstream refresh token | Gateway owns model mapping, streaming/Responses/WebSocket/account/feature compatibility and availability. Potentially useful, but not automatically necessary or Daybreak-capable. |

Source evidence already identifies a packaged personal `codex-lb`, separate from
Snajpa's pool. Its nginx entry point blocks inference paths; that does not prove
local internal API access is blocked. This is pinned configuration/source
evidence, not installed-image equivalence, a ready endpoint or permission to
expose it.
Reusing it may be smaller than a new broker if it supports the exact target,
but generic OpenAI compatibility or a listed model name does not establish
Daybreak access. The gateway must preserve the required model/account mapping,
client scopes, transport and feature/access-program metadata. Details and exact
source revisions belong to [gateway evidence](authentication-gateway-evidence.md).
Pi's `openai-codex` transport extracts account identity from an upstream JWT;
changing its base URL and supplying an ordinary gateway API key is not
automatically compatible. Select and verify the gateway-facing adapter rather
than treat the proxy as a transparent subscription login replacement.

The user's hardware-key requirement is an acceptance input. Perform the chosen
OpenAI sign-in in a real browser once for the shared Pi account/grant, **if that
flow supports the account/model**; any hardware-key challenge remains a user
interaction. Device-code or browser-callback support does not bypass MFA or
prove Daybreak support. Refresh can avoid repeated worker logins while valid,
but revocation, expiration or a recurring account challenge can require another
interactive login. Neither Pi source nor a gateway promises permanent unattended
access. No login or hardware-key prompt was attempted in this investigation.

Any shared auth service/gateway sits outside session agent cgroups as control
plane. Report its resource cost separately; per-session agent counters do not
include it. The smallest future acceptance check is shared-lock/rotation across
two disposable workers and their namespace views, then the exact browser/client/
account/model flow; keep legacy Codex under its original authority. Test gateway
inference only if that option is chosen. No credentials/token contents were
read or copied, and no live auth/model call ran. This clarification does not
justify a new authentication-platform package or a precise new effort quote.

### Durable delivery, teams and utility recovery

The current guarantee is durable prompt acceptance/reconciliation with honest
unknown outcomes. It does not mean arbitrary external tool effects happen
exactly once. Keep the same distinction in the replacement.

At the inspected Pi head, [RPC prompt handling][rpcsource] uses the command ID
only in the response, and SDK steer/follow-up enqueue can remain in memory.
Those facts do not rule out supported native-entry acceptance evidence.
The current [per-operation contract](#per-operation-admission-contract-native-witness-plus-host-receipt)
allows a positively observed native entry bound to a durable host receipt before
ACK, without requiring a native prompt UUID. A Go outbox alone or missing
history cannot supply that proof. Residual crash gaps remain Unknown/no-resend;
they do not imply a blanket ban on otherwise proved automated operations.

Pi Durable materially reduces this work: `submit(requestId)` deduplicates
admissions, documents/tasks commit together, and the [background-subagent
example][background] persists delivery/report phases. It does not supply our
roster, approvals, permission holds or lifecycle policy. In particular, the
example automatically forwards final answers, while current team members
explicitly call `report_to_lead`; preserve the latter contract. Default unsafe
tools interrupted by a crash report interruption instead of replaying effects.
Safe replay still needs operation-specific idempotency. Its default SQLite
WAL/NORMAL commits can lose the newest data on host/power failure, and the
library requires one writer per storage. Verify the selected durability mode
and process ownership before claiming parity with current full-sync receipts.

Retain stable message IDs and immutable payload/settings binding, per-recipient
queue order, cancellation, held/stopped recipients, and separate utility watcher
identity. Pi `agent_end` can precede retry/compaction/follow-up work;
`agent_settled` is the closer idle boundary, but neither alone proves an external
command completed or that its result was durably delivered. Utility launch and
report receipts remain host-owned evidence.

Current reporting trusts native `_meta.threadId`. The inspected Pi MCP path
does not provide that identity; it supplies tool arguments and progress metadata.
Bind host reporting tools to the worker's trusted conversation/member context
and recheck the current roster/session incarnation under the existing admission
locks. A model-provided `from`, slug or recipient is not an identity substitute.
Existing reporting and peer-message business logic can remain behind this
adapter. MCP is natively supported by Pi CLI; SDK loads the necessary MCP,
codemode and tool-search extensions explicitly.

### Optional questions, trusted extensions and planning

Optional questions are a distinct host capability, not Plan mode or blocking
approval. A first-party tool must commit a question with stable request ID,
immutable revision and session/member/conversation/incarnation binding, publish
the current choice/free-text card, and immediately return its pending ID. The
agent continues independent work. Preselection or elapsed time is not an answer
and does not authorize work dependent on that answer.

The browser authenticates a reply against that question/revision and commits
an immutable response ID plus pending delivery before acknowledging it. Retries
return the same receipt; corrections are ordered new responses, not silent
rewrites of an answer already used. Reconnect reconstructs the question from
host state even if the worker unloaded. A later answer goes to the original
logical recipient through ordinary durable dispatch: steer at a safe boundary,
follow-up, or eligible idle activation. Holds and stopped state remain in force.
Finished turns can still receive answers to open questions; a changed branch,
retired member or session incarnation needs explicit stale/rerouting handling.
Treat the answer as data, not a slash command or executable prompt template.

Pi's `ctx.ui` dialogs await in-memory Promise resolvers; official question
examples are TUI widgets. They do not provide this ask-and-continue contract.
SDK message injection and RPC steer/follow-up supply execution primitives, but
question/outbox receipts do not close the unresolved Pi admission crash window.
The same durable-delivery release gate applies. Detailed source and contract:
[extensions/questions evidence](extension-and-question-evidence.md).

Use supported SDK `customTools`/extensions or one small reviewed extension in
stock RPC workers for reporting, questions and mode controls. No external
extension is selected or needed here. Pin actual source/artifact and transitive
dependencies; inspect loaded code, install hooks, overrides and credential/
process access; verify maintenance and exact supported Pi version; package the
reviewed artifact reproducibly. Use ordinary checks/final review for updates,
not a new approval process. Managed workers should not float-install executable
extensions or silently skip required host tools; preserve intended instruction
and skill discovery. Official examples establish provenance, not portal trust
or recovery parity.

The upstream Plan example disables built-in edit/write and regex-filters bash
while retaining other active tools. That is not enforceable read-only planning:
custom/MCP/nested tools and shell programs can still mutate state.

Preserve the current Plan workflow and its promised restrictions as trusted
host state. Stronger strict read-only enforcement beyond that existing contract
is a product decision, not automatic migration scope. If required, such a
read-only planning profile must restrict
every enabled tool family and delegated task, including codemode/MCP, and avoid
arbitrary shell execution rather than try to prove shell programs safe with
regex. Bind “implement plan” to the accepted plan's immutable identity/digest
and receipt, as today. Test restart, stale plan, duplicate click and queued work.
Pi has no built-in OS permission boundary. The current installed policy grants
full execution access, but any required restricted profile must have a real
host/process enforcement design. This does not change the trusted-local-operator
model or require protecting against the host administrator.

### Persistence, coexistence and recovery

Use a backend-tagged binding for new sessions and retain original Codex session,
queue, receipt and rollout evidence. Never reinterpret a Codex thread ID as a
Pi session ID. An unresolved old operation must be reconciled by its original
supported backend; creating a Pi session cannot settle it.

For future migration/retirement decisions, the choices are materially different.
Only side-by-side new Pi sessions are in the initial implementation plan; no
continuation converter or transfer/cutover machinery is to be built now:

| Route | Existing-session usability | Cost and recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Side-by-side, new Pi sessions | Existing sessions keep full Codex execution and recovery | Recommended first step. Two pinned backend adapters/test matrices remain, with additional Pi process/storage cost during coexistence. |
| Derive a new Pi development session | Original Codex session stays fully usable; Pi receives an attributed context summary or transformed completed messages | Smallest independent continuation. New ownership/resources must be assigned explicitly; copying context does not transfer worktrees, claims or completion obligations. |
| Derive a Pi conversation within the same development session | Preserve initiative/Git/resource identity and the activatable original Codex conversation | Needs deliberate handover with one active execution authority per member, source/target mapping and effect reconciliation before switching either way. This is not lossless migration. |
| Full-fidelity session migration | Would need equivalent history, members, queues, goals, pending tools, receipts and recovery, including retained archives | Not established. Pi's JSONL import reads Pi sessions; it is not a Codex execution-state converter. No reliable effort quote without a supported fidelity contract and fixtures. |
| Remove Codex | Old sessions remain usable only if every required execution/recovery dependency has a proved replacement | Reject as the first step. A read-only history viewer, new default or successful new Pi session does not meet the requirement. |

Retirement additionally needs supported archive/restore paths that cannot
reintroduce an unsupported Codex dependency. Preserve the old executable,
protocol adapter and state readers while writable sessions or uncertain native
operations need them. No stop/removal/cleanup is authorized by this design.
The tradeoff is ongoing dual-backend maintenance in exchange for avoiding a
high-risk mandatory migration. Keep the legacy adapter stable and generalize
only the shared portal contract. Source-backed route and state details are in
[coexistence evidence](coexistence-evidence.md).

Coding-agent v3 JSONL migration and Pi Durable storage are different formats;
opening legacy files can rewrite them. Keep original data and test selected
readers/writers before touching retained history. Preserve source attribution
and explicit omissions in any derived continuation; hidden reasoning and native
execution state do not transfer merely because text/tool output can be imported.

Current workspace software recovery is **forward-only**. Do not promise that
an older package can be selected after new state is written. A corrected newer
package may disable new Pi creation while retaining readers and recovery for
both backends. Routing future sessions back to a supported Codex backend is a
product fallback, not permission to downgrade storage or overwrite receipts.
Extend the installed runtime/package capability fences so incompatible packages
refuse state they cannot preserve. Existing lifecycle journals, exact final-head
rules, resource ownership and recovery commands remain authoritative.

No application database/API/client changes to vpsAdmin, its Terraform provider,
or vpsAdminOS node protocols are proposed. Mixed-version concerns here are the
portal, runtime helpers, agent service, browser clients and persisted session
state. A later rollout must retain old browser/API recovery behavior or require
an explicit refresh without duplicating an accepted operation.

## Historical estimate and current allocation

[implementation-plan.md](implementation-plan.md) now owns the complete future
packages, file owners, dependencies, release gates and checks. The earlier
candidate table is superseded. The main plan did not itself assign work; the
current ARCH-EXEC briefs above record boundaries for lead-allocated initial
implementation after user authorization. The current plan distinguishes a usable manual pilot from the stronger
automation gate, with independent seam/UI work proceeding when safe.

Package A's narrower web/team/lifecycle parity estimate was **30–60 engineer-days,
roughly 6–12 working weeks for one experienced engineer**. The newly requested
session supervisor/namespace/tmp accounting, optional questions and per-member
fallback add real scope; that estimate is a baseline, not an all-in quote for E.
Those historical estimates are not additive. Resolve supported admission and namespace/permission mechanisms
before giving a revised total: a narrow integration differs materially from a
new privileged launcher or maintained harness fork. The first 3–5 day prototype
is a decision timebox, not a promise that every expanded acceptance case fits.
Do not presume two implementers halve elapsed time across these dependencies.

Those bands assume the existing endpoint/accounts work, a supported admission
solution exists, old sessions coexist rather than convert, and ordinary portal
workflows are preserved. Unverified authentication/entitlement and missing model
feature parity are exclusions, not zero-cost tasks; external provider refusals
may block feasibility rather than add predictable engineering days. An SDK fork,
new generalized harness, broad history conversion or reproducing unsupported
subscription reset APIs invalidates the estimate. Optional same-live-session
CLI attachment is a separate approximately 5–10 day exploration/implementation
after the owner protocol is stable; it is not on the web migration's critical
path. Historical import effort remains unestimated without a defined fidelity
contract and representative retained fixtures.

## Resource use: stored history is different from running agents

The user added a resource comparison after the capability investigation.
Implementer0 owns the bounded aggregate observations in
[resource-evidence.md](resource-evidence.md). The figures below are reconciled
with that completed package-D artifact; native process memory was sampled at
22:14:56 UTC on 2026-11-11, with other observations near 22:14–22:18 UTC.
No Pi benchmark has run, so numerical claims about Pi RAM, CPU, startup latency,
throughput or savings would be unsupported.

| Observed current population or resource | Meaning and limit |
| --- | --- |
| 83 current tracking directories + 343 archived = 426 dated sessions | Directory classification, not active-agent count. Four non-date directories are excluded. |
| Public session listing: 432 known rows, 60 with managed tmux | A broader known-slug union than the directory count. A terminal attachment/session does not establish active model work. |
| Dedicated Codex home: 4,190 stored threads, 2,213 unarchived / 1,977 archived | Of these, 3,667 match this workspace's session-cwd prefix, across 205 distinct cwds. Stored/unarchived is not loaded or active. |
| Shared native daemon: 6.50 GiB PSS; 91 reporting helpers: 0.78 GiB aggregate PSS | Process-memory observations. Helpers are separate processes, not proof of 91 active agents or retained roster members. |
| Code-mode host: 0.054 GiB PSS; portal Go: 0.108 GiB; child naming Codex: 0.218 GiB | Separate observed components; not a complete host or all-agent memory total. |
| Native cgroup: 34.20 GiB, including approximately 24.05 GiB file cache | Cgroup charge is not daemon heap or private resident memory. |
| Rollout files: approximately 17.26 GiB; native thread-history SQLite: 5.86 GiB | Persistent disk footprint, not RAM. Coexistence must retain supported original recovery/history data. |

The attributed native-service processes total approximately **7.34 GiB PSS**.
Thirteen other Codex processes are excluded because workload ownership was not
established; this is not a host-wide total. Measurements are live observations
at nearby times, not one atomic or idle-baseline snapshot. The evidence artifact
retains raw units, observed store paths and collection methods; installed source
equivalence was not proved by those executable paths alone.

Loaded conversation count, active model-call count and retained-member count
remain unknown; no peer roster/transcript contents were read. These limits
prevent a defensible per-agent memory estimate or a numeric Pi savings claim.
The practical conclusion is still strong: thousands of stored threads must not
force thousands of permanent Pi processes or loaded histories. Use loaded
lead/member workers inside each session's supervisor boundary and evaluate safe
idle unloading. The earlier shared-SDK saving hypothesis is superseded by the
chosen worker topology. More process baselines may cost memory; retained
histories, extensions, MCP helpers and isolation still need measurement.

| Population or cost | Expected architectural comparison |
| --- | --- |
| Open or archived session records | Mainly persisted history/metadata. An archived session does not require a Node process or loaded AgentSession. Open-but-idle records can also be unloaded. Counts alone do not establish RAM demand. |
| Loaded conversations and retained members | Both candidate implementations use SDK or RPC worker processes for loaded members within one session boundary. Node/package overhead can repeat; dormant retained members need no permanent worker. Do not assume SDK workers are smaller without measurement. |
| Active model/tool work | Provider latency, concurrency, tool processes and builds can dominate. Replacing the harness does not eliminate this work; multi-provider concurrency can increase total usage. |
| Long histories | Coding-agent SessionManager holds entries and indexes in memory when loaded; keeping many long histories loaded can be expensive. Pi Durable explicitly recommends SQLite over its all-history-in-memory JSONL backend for long-running agents. Measure history paging/reconstruction as well as idle process RSS. |
| Process isolation | Worker processes separate event loops and some failures; the cgroup/namespace and supervisor are shared only within the development session. A session-wide memory limit or supervisor failure can affect every member. This is ownership/accounting, not a hostile-member security guarantee. |
| Migration coexistence | Keeping Codex available for old histories plus the Pi service can initially increase baseline memory and retained disk. Retiring native history/recovery dependencies is a separate later decision, not an assumed immediate saving. |

The source basis is the [SDK session ownership contract][sdk],
[SessionManager's in-memory entry indexes][sessionmanager], and [Pi Durable's
storage documentation][durablestorage]. These establish plausible cost drivers,
not a measured ranking against Codex. Independent runtime/provider refresh
timers, catalog/auth caches and browser subscriptions may keep otherwise idle
processes alive; the prototype should count them rather than infer “idle” from
an empty composer.

A later comparison should hold provider/model, tool workload, transcript size
and active concurrency constant. Record cold service baseline, one short/long
loaded history, the representative retained team, reconnect, and idle unload;
measure aggregate PSS/RSS, CPU, startup/reconnect latency and storage growth.
Use the current aggregate session/thread counts to select a representative
population, not to launch every archived thread. Separate model/tool subprocess
cost from harness cost and avoid double-counting shared pages. This can be part
of the decision prototype; it is not permission to run one now.

Design milestone 2026-11-13; base D
`e0925346dae8e862df518b3fecc6e857561c1000`, C
`5aa6111db1a71b17191befb8532bad7dcae2e15d`. This supersedes the preceding
follow-up's missing-contract conclusion as a proposed implementation brief,
not as evidence of implemented or tested public support. Lead requested this
necessary opt-in product join after accepting that conclusion. Architect0 retains
Astra/xhigh/workspace_write. Owner2/architect2 supplied exact public/preparation
facts; owner1 supplied pinned builtin model, SDK transport and Node trust facts.
No application/test edits or execution occurred in this design pass.

**Release boundary and owner.** This is one complete prospective implementer2
package, after lead confirms capacity and accepts this brief: one new isolated
successor worktree of exact D, its own branch/index/build outputs and disposable
fixtures. Keep C unchanged. Owner0's three host checks on immutable e092 and
all existing candidate/CI receipts remain independent and untouched. Implementer
owns public join, compatibility scanner, tests, technical documentation, commits,
quick results and ensuing fixes together; no partial public enablement before its
preparation reader/target fence exists. Lead owns allocation, visible copy,
independent review and each later expensive-check release. No repository/machine
claim or application/profile deployment follows from this design.

**Conventional public path.** Preserve authenticated/origin-checked POST /sessions,
withCreationMutation's existing transition SH/current-profile admission, and the
existing request-ID preparation/status/retry routes. Parse backend exactly once:
omitted/empty/codex means the original Codex path; pi requires the request-ID path
and all Pi-specific fields/admission; other values, duplicates and contradictory
fields refuse before acceptance. The old name-only Codex route is unchanged;
name-only Pi refuses rather than acquiring a second creation protocol. Fork/Plan
creation and existing Codex provider routes remain unchanged.

Render an ordinary backend control in the existing new-session form with Codex
selected by default. Offer Pi from the actual valid production composition,
selected immutable package/profile, complete creation/workflow/role/preparation
capabilities and installed Solo preset. Page rendering performs local reads only;
it is neither provider entitlement nor dispatched-provider evidence. Use sanitized
Catalog.Public summaries and the composition's validated package Default to show
the fixed primary provider plus its supported model/thinking choices. There is
no existing Pi catalog HTTP route and none is needed. Do not reuse /api/models or
/api/codex-providers to authorize Pi. Package provider/account, full fallback
order/categories/budget remain fixed by existing initialPolicy; browser model and
thinking override only that primary as already supported. Filter choices through
the owning selection validator, including finite route evidence and account
projection, not labels alone. No arbitrary provider/account picker or new gateway
configuration is introduced.

Pi requires an explicitly selected installed Solo (one lead, no members), a valid
explicit custom name, nonempty text, explicit supported model/thinking and no
upload scope/attachments or nonempty Codex provider field. Name-only here means
the form's custom-name field, not the legacy no-request-ID protocol. This first
Pi path never calls the Codex naming utility, invents a name or silently drops
files. Preserve sensitivity and browser-notification preferences in the frozen
input and normal handoff. Keep Codex's optional name, auto naming, all existing
uploads, default team/model behavior and original18 VM assertions intact. Pi
selection must not silently replace a non-Solo roster. Lead finalizes the brief
Pi-only name/text limitation and unavailable-capability copy in context.

Expose a Pi-only opaque `piProviderDigest` in the rendered form: SHA256 of a
versioned deterministic owning encoding of the catalog's exact raw Digest and
the complete detached package Default selection. It reveals no credential refs.
Submit it alongside backend=pi and the existing team catalogDigest. It is a
staleness token, never authority. Freeze after validating against the actual
composition under existing transition admission. Reject stale Pi configuration
before the first accepting save with a distinct preacceptance result; do not
reuse the existing team-catalog unlock code unless its exact proof applies.
Ordinary failures keep the saved browser body locked. The user can start a
separate request through the existing explicit action.

**Preparation wire and original ownership.** Keep schema1/inputVersion1 for all
Codex preparations, including byte-identical old JSON/digest behavior. Normalize
explicit codex to the existing omitted representation; new Pi-only optional
fields must be omitted from Codex input/snapshot JSON. Introduce only the Pi arm:
schema2/inputVersion2, input.backend=pi, input.piProviderDigest, and an optional
snapshot Pi object containing the exact catalog Digest and complete detached
package Default selection. Version2 binds backend and Pi token into InputDigest;
SnapshotDigest also binds those pure package inputs and the exact saved preset,
including literal LeadInstructions. Reject mixed schemas/versions/backend/fields,
unknown fields, duplicate keys and malformed values. The terminal schema2 mapping
retains schema/inputVersion/InputDigest/original IDs even after Snapshot/Handoff
are compacted; therefore Pi identity cannot disappear with receipt retirement.
No migration or rewrite of schema1 records is required or allowed.

Fresh admission validates available real Pi composition, exact current immutable
root/profile, complete metadata and explicit Solo/role plus pure desired
selection BEFORE accepting-record publication, upload claims, reservations or
native effects. A small private pure selection-validation extraction in
pi_providers.go may share initialPolicy's existing target checks; do not fabricate
session/member IDs to call a session policy validator. Freeze catalog/default,
preset and settings before acceptance. During later handoff, recheck current
admission and exact frozen catalog/default equality, then use the real newly
reserved identities with existing initialPolicy/FreezePiCreationSelection. A
changed package provider/default or unavailable saved selection holds the original
request; it never replaces selection, instructions, goal or IDs. Existing original
root receipt takes precedence over recomputing current configuration. No stale
preparation may fall through into a different backend.

Input-digest replay lookup must precede fresh Pi catalog/availability checks so a
lost acknowledgement can still identify its original request after configuration
changes. Read/status of a saved record remains possible; any resumed effect still
passes its appropriate current and frozen checks. Keep original receiptID,
requestID, attempts, timestamps, destination slug/epoch, upload ownership and
uncertain-save confirmation discipline. The Pi empty-upload path preserves raw
Goal through the existing text preparation semantics without creating a claim.
preparationCreationRequest carries backend=pi only for schema2; its schema2
receipt matcher requires original schema4 request/preset/receipt/epoch and the
exact frozen provider selection. The old schema1 receipt matcher keeps its
original1/3 behavior. Status/page may expose backend=pi; omission is accepted only
for legacy Codex. Retry/name requests still supply original receipt/attempt, never
a replacement backend/settings payload. Pi has a frozen explicit name, so it
does not acquire Codex naming recovery or a canSetName offer. Completed historical instructionless Pi
proof remains readable; incomplete legacy instructionless recovery still cannot
advance on an empty role digest. Original Accepted/Unknown/native-started
Lookup-only/no-replacement-Send fences in existing R4 are unchanged.

**Necessary pre-root compatibility fence.** Schema2 Pi preparation is genuinely
incompatible with the strict e092 preparation reader before any root receipt
exists. Existing piCreationSchema4 and provider-policy scans do not cover it.
Add exact integer `piPreparationSchema:2` to the whole runtime metadata only with
the complete reader/caller/guard implementation; use a bounded duplicate-rejecting
owning decoder, rejecting absent/wrong/noninteger values for new Pi admission.
The new web store export `InspectRetainedPiPreparations(ctx, stateRoot, workspaces)`
returns only sorted unique `{workspace,requestId}` references to schema2 records.
It shares the actual readPreparation/validatePreparation and store traversal
semantics; it does not construct NewContext, pause records, write state, create a
parallel permissive parser or manufacture a session incarnation.

Inspect BOTH session-preparations and session-preparation-mappings, including a
terminal record awaiting its ordinary directory move. Retain existing private
uid/mode/O_NOFOLLOW/size/filename/digest/state checks, duplicate-ID rejection and
per-workspace 512 unfinished/10000 mapping/aggregate limits, plus the existing
whole-command output bound. Preserve the store's recognized
unpublished atomic-temp handling; those files do not establish logical acceptance.
Inventory the portal namespace, not just directories reached from existing root
bindings: accepting records may have no slug, and compact mappings may outlive
root receipts. Every Pi reference must map to the canonical registered workspace
and exact portal directory identity. Orphan Pi preparation, malformed/mixed or
unreadable authoritative input refuses; absent namespaces are ordinary absence.
The empty-registry path must inspect preparation subdirectories too. Do not reject
unrelated portal entries or reinterpret valid legacy-only preparation semantics
merely to discover Pi state. Preserve the safe generic-parent/private-child mode
contract already corrected in D.

Extend the EXISTING executing-package pi-team-preflight pipeline with an
independent pre-root arm: no Pi preparations retains its schema1 output; with
any Pi preparation return schema2 `{schema,required,sessions,piPreparations}`.
`required` keeps its existing meaning (nonempty session claims); piPreparations
is a nonempty bounded, sorted, unique list of the above exact references. The
Ruby decoder accepts these two strict arms, validates workspace/UUID identities,
and retains ALL existing session-claim/native-creation-fence checks unchanged.
Preparation references require the new target preparation scalar plus the existing
complete Pi creation/workflow/role support; they confer no ready/native authority.
Do not add a fake session source kind, relax retained_creation_fence!, or treat a
scalar as proof that stored bytes are valid.

Wire this through require_compatible_session_backends!, including its no-roots
branch, before candidate installation and its existing post-wait/activation
rechecks under transition EX. For zero registered workspaces retain the current
Ruby require_empty_team_namespaces! checks and permit the existing child command
to receive zero --workspace solely for the new preparation orphan inventory. Its
zero-root branch runs that owning inspection and returns an empty schema1 result
only on proven absence of Pi preparations; do not feed zero roots through existing
native inspectors that require registered scopes or invent a placeholder root. The scanner remains the actual executing package's
bin/workspace-portal derived from package_root, with its existing 30s/4MiB/4096-byte
bounds and child join. The candidate is the target being checked, not a scanner
substitute. New preparation publication stays under the existing transition SH;
async writes retain original admission ordering. This closes the pre-root gap
without another command/framework or ledger. Forward-only package recovery stays
forward-only. Old binaries reject schema2; neither compaction nor deleting a root
makes them compatible while a schema2 mapping remains. Preserve records and use a
newer compatible reader; no record stripping/conversion or forced rollback.

**Browser durability.** Existing saved schema2/3 drafts and schema-less text
imports retain Codex meaning; attempted IDs, scope, selection and body bytes are
never rebuilt or appended with backend. Keep new ordinary Codex drafts schema3.
Use schema4 only for Pi drafts, with exact pi backend/token/model/thinking and
one backend=pi in the frozen body. Old browsers must reject it. Preserve
freeze-before-first-POST/readback, original GET-status/identical-POST recovery,
receipt/attempt/time identity and the sole existing exact team-catalog rejection
unlock. Capability loss never resets a saved Pi draft to Codex. Browser backend
change is available only while editable. All delayed Codex catalog responses must
still match backend and selection epoch; provider-change/reset events cannot
overwrite Pi selections. Suppress the unsupported Codex CLI preview in Pi mode.

Unmount Pi uploads completely, including automatic draft allocation. Switching
from Codex with selected files refuses until the user explicitly removes them or
starts a separate request. Switching with an empty unused scope may detach that
scope on explicit selection, leaving its normal expiry untouched; it must not
serialize it as Pi or delete pending files. Switching back uses normal Codex
upload setup. Do not weaken locked-form/storage-failure recovery.

**Honest offline provider.** One focused Pi arm in existing
nix/tests/session-creation.nix, test/creation_acceptance_browser.cjs and

The package adds supported immutable piProviderConfig with one builtin native
openai/API-key account, one validated builtin gpt-4o-mini model (openai-responses,
reasoning=false), thinking off and the existing allowed finite route evidence.
No fallback dispatch is claimed. Ordinary production NewContext must construct

Stored auth.json contains only the fixture's synthetic native openai API key.
Never inject Runtime, Host, Dial, savedStart, fixed production IDs, catalog binder,

Control builtin https://api.openai.com/v1 in the disposable guest with hosts/DNS
to loopback, a local HTTPS443 listener and certificate SAN api.openai.com signed

SSL_CERT_FILE. The pinned worker Node22.23.2 is built with
--openssl-use-def-ca-store/--shared-openssl, and the production worker preserves
SSL_CERT_FILE; verify the actual new package pi-worker.json Node identity and
observed trust before public creation. NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE alone is not that proof.
Do not disable verification or introduce NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS,
wrappers or production endpoint APIs. Permit no unintended external provider
traffic from the guest. This tests a builtin endpoint under controlled DNS/TLS;
it does not establish user-facing custom-gateway configuration. RuntimeConfigRef
remains builtin. The accepted lack of fresh-agent models projection is not solved
or advertised as gateway support by this fixture.

Extend the deterministic Responses handler with actual Pi-compatible created,
output_item.done and completed events: matching response/item IDs, output_index,

An incomplete/malformed stream must not be relabeled Accepted completion.

Use go test -mod=readonly with exact nonzero new/affected selectors, existing
Node test files, Ruby host/backend test selectors, node --check and git diff

Prefer ONE publication of the reviewed public-feature branch and its automatic
Check run, instead of a local full creation run followed by the same automatic
run. Exact d441 .github/workflows/check.yml triggers on every push with no branch

(the default devWorkspace package), Ruby/focused checks and pi-worker. Archive
runs the existing session-archive-lifecycle check; creation runs the existing

maintenance subtests in order, followed by the19th builtin Pi Solo public-form/
cold-portal-reconnect subtest and its final writable-Codex follow-up. Host runs
only on workflow_dispatch or master push; a feature push explicitly SKIPS
host-module-idempotency, session-recovery-boot and pi-runtime-host. Their older
e092 results remain baseline evidence, not tests of the new closure. Do not add

and the intended feature ref under the Git procedure; confirm the recorded

The capacity-confirmed CI owner/fresh watcher binds the automatic run ID, attempt,

Accept only authoritative terminal success for fast/archive/creation plus raw

11 original subtests and creation's18 original subtests plus Pi19, including the
actual Node/TLS probe, visible Pi creation, original receipt/Goal/role/Accepted
identity, cold portal PID change and unchanged original proof, reconnect and
post-Pi writable Codex. Keep existing per-assertion deadlines and failure exports;

fresh execution. Jobs run independently: one failure need not terminate the

this estimate is not a raised test timeout. Missing progress, unexpected expensive

lead with evidence; no automatic retry, guessed fixture fix or deadline inflation.

   probe. Before request, print/persist only version/execPath, process.versions.openssl,
   filtered report sharedObjects for libssl/libcrypto, two CA paths/realpaths/hashes,

### Public Pi/codex-lb compatibility research — 2026-11-16

Public upstream is [Soju06/codex-lb](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb),
confirmed by its repository, documentation and package provenance. This identifies
the public project, not our deployed gateway revision or transport mode. Read-only
GitHub issue/PR searches covered Pi plus codex-lb, Responses, unsupported_value,
parallel_tool_calls, reasoning and tools; exact status/dates were checked through
the public repository API. No private route details entered searches.

Compatibility is reported, with important path/version limits:

- [Pi #5152](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5152), opened May 28,
  triaged **not planned** June 19, last updated September 8, reports Pi using
  codex-lb's `/v1` endpoint with hangs/errors. Its proposal concerns opaque bearer
  keys on the different `openai-codex-responses` adapter. The linked
  [user patch set](https://github.com/lkraider/pi-codex-lb-patches) is not merged
  upstream support and also changes retries/affinity/history resend. Do not adopt
  it under this trial's native-adapter and no-resend contracts. Pinned Pi1.5.2
  still calls extractAccountId unconditionally on that Codex adapter; our existing
  `openai-responses` API-key path does not have that specific JWT requirement.
- [codex-lb #1166](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/1166), closed unmerged
  as superseded July 10, reports successful Pi streamed text and function tools
  with GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra through `openai-completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`
  after #1161. This is useful affirmative user evidence, not verification of
  our pinned Pi, GPT-6.1 Sol/high or native Responses route. No adapter switch is
  selected. The [client guide](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/blob/main/docs/client-setup.md)
  (last changed October 16) documents general OpenAI-compatible bearer-key setup,
  but supplies no exact Pi1.5.2/Sol-high acceptance guarantee.
- Merged [#1161](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/1161) July 10 preserves
  additional_tools and derives transport-specific Lite signaling; merged
  [#1200](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/1200) July 11 prevents injected
  top-level tools:[] when the client omitted it. Both shipped in1.21.0 July 15.
  These are relevant to pinned Pi's actual additional_tools request shape, but
  installed inclusion and the third failure's connection are unknown.
- [#1411](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/issues/1411) reports unsupported_value
  when Lite reasoning.context is not all_turns. Its fix
  [#1431](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/1431) merged July 22 and shipped
  in1.22.0 July 24. It normalizes context only after trusted Lite selection and
  preserves effort. Pinned Pi's generic serializer supplies effort/summary, with
  high potentially carried by configuration_update; it does not supply this
  context itself. This is a gateway-mode prerequisite to verify, not evidence
  that our effective high was wrong or that this caused the opaque rejection.
- [#2531](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/2531), opened September 28,
  updated November 13, remains **open/unmerged**. It proposes literal false for
  parallel_tool_calls only on Lite upstream requests; non-Lite is unchanged.
  [#2465](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/issues/2465), open since September 19,
  reports this on1.25.0-beta.9 with Factory/Droid, including image bypass.
  Thus neither boolean is a universal proxy compatibility rule. These reports
  do not identify our second/third failure or authorize toggling the setting.
- [#1569](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/issues/1569), opened August 2 and
  closed August 11, specifically reports Pi native compaction and unsupported
  prompt_cache_options; the maintainer says the fix shipped in1.23.0 August 11.
  Our bounded probes disabled compaction, so it is not a matched first cause.
  Release attribution above follows the upstream
  [changelog](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

The extension comparison is deliberate: pinned Pi supports input transforms,
custom tools, lifecycle hooks and `setSessionName`, and the runtime already uses
trusted inline factories for tool policy. `noExtensions:true` disables ambient
extensions; it does not prohibit those explicit factories. A future model-facing
behavior may belong in an extension case by case. None of these browser,
preparation or host-boundary corrections requires enabling arbitrary extension
loading. SDK/TUI render hooks also do not render this web portal.

### Upload contract, including the osctl ct top screenshots

`portal/internal/uploads/store.go:950–1002` already freezes ordered file IDs,
user text and an effective text prompt listing private absolute paths. Reuse
that exact owning preparation path. Files live outside the repository under

0400, drafts expire after seven days, and accepted references retain files.
Current store limits are 50 files, 1 GiB/file, 2 GiB/prompt, 10 GiB/session and
100 GiB/workspace, with 4 MiB upload chunks. These are storage limits, **not**

The pinned SDK's `core/tools/read.js:203–235` detects image bytes and returns

The existing service is a separate naming-only **Codex App Server** using the

### Ready-session runtime upgrade: sufficient bounded implementation brief

Lead has allocated the necessary upgrade correction after confirming the missing
production path. Owner2's display commit5b3163eb is closed and remains a separate
presentation-only change. This package upgrades one explicitly selected ready Pi
session to the selected application package; it does not upgrade all sessions,
recreate a session, resume original creation or replay any user input.

**Source cause.** At a43, `pi_runtime.go` accepts only supervise; production Ensure
is reached from initial creation only. `Controller.Unload/Load`, H0 Stop and
`prepareSuccessor` exist, but are not composed into an ordinary ready-session
operation. `session/backend_publication.go:114–141` deliberately refuses generation
replacement. A new generation also needs the real portal attachment before Load:
`conversation.go:313–316` takes its host-tool set from that attachment. No operator
script, empty host-tool set, service restart or direct helper call completes this
contract. The following connection is the minimum owning correction.

**Ordinary entry.** Extend the already registered `workspace-portal pi-runtime`
command with `upgrade`, an HTTP client for the existing private portal Unix
socket. Required explicit inputs identify workspace, slug, one request UUID and
expected predecessor generation; the CLI also receives the normal portal socket
and origin. It sends the same bounded request to
`POST /api/sessions/<slug>/pi-runtime-upgrade`; the portal resolves its own selected
package/profile and all native identities. No browser/CLI-provided helper, native
history path, model, credentials or target package is authoritative. Use existing
exact-origin, private-socket and session-operation admission. The handler is a
normal portal operation, not a new daemon/bridge. A matching readonly status route
may return this existing runtime request's status after a lost HTTP response;
it cannot create an upgrade. Repeating the original POST uses the same UUID and
expectation, never an automatic new ID. Completed replay is observational.

**State and orchestration.** Reuse `runtime.json` schema2's immutable request
history as the sole durable upgrade intent. Factor its existing successor
reservation so the explicit upgrader can save the complete selected StartRequest,
new generation and CurrentRequestID with phase `preparing` **before Unload/Stop**.
Keep the predecessor entry, original launch/config/root and original creation
records untouched. This uses existing fields/formats: no upgrade ledger, extra
journal, per-command marker, worker protocol bump or additional phase flag.
Ordinary Ensure retains its existing stopped-predecessor guard and cannot drain a
runtime. Only the explicit upgrader owns the pre-drain reservation. Its new current
request makes ordinary old-generation Manager calls stale; recovery reads the
same stored StartRequest/previous request, not current defaults.

Expose one Manager Upgrade operation with small typed portal hooks for actual
host attachment and final authority publication. Its ordered work is:

1. Under normal selected-profile/transition admission, prove the unchanged ready
   binding/authority/original creation identity; capture the current runtime and
   bound member set. Validate the selected package with the existing validator,
   exact account bindings, saved model/thinking/settings/instructions/tool policy,
   and original request expectation. Require current workers idle with no pending
   input, callbacks, Unknown effects or active resources; reject unrelated utility
   or unbound loaded work instead of draining it opportunistically. Attach the
   predecessor through the portal's existing `ensureAttachment` when needed.
2. Reserve the same-instance successor request as `preparing` using existing
   runtime-record construction and durable package retention. This is the frozen
   intent before the first effect. Subsequent calls must match it exactly.
3. Unload only the captured bound workers through their existing unload semantics.
   The private upgrade path may address its **exact proven predecessor** despite
   the newly reserved current pointer: verify its immutable request, live helper
   observation/handshake and process identity before the private controller call.
   Do not relax public Inspect/handleCall to permit historical dispatch. An already
   unloaded mapping needs its existing positive completion evidence; a disappeared
   loaded worker is Unknown, not a successful unload.
4. Use a narrow optional host Stop capability implemented by nativeHost with the
   existing fixed H0 helper protocol. Do not enlarge every Controller fake or add
   raw shell/systemctl fallback. Stop the exact predecessor request, then reuse
   `validTerminalReceipt`, current cgroup drain and `assertRuntimeSettled` before
   ordinary successor preparation/Start. Native/helper uncertainty remains held.
5. Run existing successor preparation/start/inspection for that saved request.
   Reuse its retained roots, descriptor lock order, same-ID semantics and handshake.
   Once it is ready, invoke the **portal-owned** new-generation `ensureAttachment`
   hook and wait for its existing initial ACK. Only then Load the same bound native
   conversations. Require unchanged native ID/history reference, effective saved
   settings, instructions and tool policy; no Create, Send or Configure occurs.
6. Publish ready authority for the new generation using a separate proof-bound CAS,
   and invalidate old portal workflow observations. Compare the exact old authority
   and unchanged binding revision; accept only the verified current successor chain,
   complete predecessor drain, new runtime handshake and matching loaded members.
   Keep PublishPiRuntimeAuthority's existing same-generation semantics unchanged.
   Return a safe status containing request/generation/package identity and outcome.

The private predecessor-control allowance is only for draining the captured
predecessor of this preparing request. It must not become a public historical
runtime dispatch interface. Preserve the core lock order: transition SH, session
runtime EX, manager runtime.lock. Reuse the existing locks; no extra lock store.
The handler owns the session lock for the operation and releases everything on
return/cancellation. Do not hold launch.lock across helper calls. Initial/workflow
invalidation ACKs are the existing cache/attachment path, not domain tool execution;
prove their progress under the actual held locks in the joined fixture. No domain
callback may require servicing during the operation because pending callbacks and
native work refused admission. If an actual ACK path acquires the same session
lock, stop that edit and use a short release/recheck around that wait with the
reserved current-generation fence still authoritative; never disable the ACK.

**Partial retry and admission.** Once reserved, normal portal session mutations
must compare authority generation with the existing CurrentRuntimeReader; mismatch
is an upgrade in progress, not permission to use the old handle. Reuse that one
owning admission check; only this exact operation's recovery accepts its reserved
successor. The existing retained-runtime preflight must reject an unfinished
successor/current-authority mismatch before a package transition. It uses the
owning runtime reader, not a second Ruby interpretation of native state.

A crash after reservation leaves the original request preparing. Reissue that
request to inspect/reconcile each existing mapping/host receipt and proceed only
on positive completion. Same-ID host Stop is idempotent; old terminal Stop cannot
affect a successor. Once the new request is `starting`, preserve Ensure's ordinary
Inspect-only behavior: absent/uncertain host intent does not authorize another
Start. Lost Load/publication replies reconcile the existing current mapping and
proof; do not restart a loaded/unknown worker or restore overwritten files.
A crash after ready publication returns the completed result after revalidation.

For new delivery modes, retry:true is a strict same-ID ENQUIRY, never enqueue on
missing receipt. It compares saved exact text/mode/identity, reads original frozen
settings and digest, and returns live Pending/Accepted/NotSubmitted/Unknown. A
missing/unproved record is Unknown, not permission to dispatch. Preserve immutable
original Input.Retry and digest; do not recompute an original false input as true.
A changed delivery under the same ID conflicts. Encode new modes in reserved
ordinary interactive ActionContext values `pi-delivery-v1:steer` and
`pi-delivery-v1:followUp`, so the existing schema1 Input/digest format remains exact;
reject a supplied conflicting ActionContext. Old inputs/digests are unchanged.
Internal creation/workflow/utility sends retain their existing absent-mode path.

**Admission and native acceptance.** Existing session/workflow/settings/tool/access
checks and attachment preparation still precede durable intent. Serialize each
short enqueue under existing locks; write prepared then dispatching in the existing
receipt owner before native invocation. A bounded in-memory registry in the same
supervisor/worker tracks at most20 admitted pending inputs by original ID plus
immutable input and exact worker identity. This is execution state, not another
ledger. It permits successive admitted inputs, including a steer after an already
acknowledged followUp; a truly unresolved/Unknown receipt continues to fence new
inputs. Capacity refusal before native enqueue is honest NotSubmitted.

Worker constructs the literal native user message and binds its OBJECT identity to
the input operation before synchronous public `session.agent.steer(message)` or
`followUp(message)`. These are declared public Agent APIs, preserve that object and
use normal AgentSession event persistence/continuation. Do not access private SDK
queues, expand templates or manually append history. Validate exclusive ownership
of native queued objects using public peekQueuedMessages; unexpected foreign queued
objects hold. Streaming choice and queue insertion have no intervening await.
When native is idle, use normal `session.prompt` with expandPromptTemplates:false
and existing exact initial-user proof; an idle race must not strand a lower-level
queue without a running loop. Keep native/tool/account/instruction policy guards;
queueing cannot reconfigure them. AgentSession's private text queue labels and
pendingMessageCount are not operation authority.

An exact worker enqueue acknowledgement yields Pending, never Accepted. Return it
and release web session EX, C mutation lock, conversation c.mu and receipt mutex;
none may remain held awaiting model/tool completion or consumed input. The supervisor
owns a completion task tied to its lifetime and that exact registered operation,
using a narrow worker input-wait/result operation or typed input event. It holds
no effect/admission mutex while waiting. Browser disconnect/30s HTTP timeout does
not cancel an already proven live enqueue; same-ID enquiry can recover it. An
uncertain enqueue result retains Unknown/held and never re-enqueues. No unbounded
HTTP extension or lock exception; worker completion remains bounded by20 registered
inputs and must settle on shutdown/abort. Final receipt writes take short locks.

At consumption, public user message_end must be the exact owned object; after the
SDK append boundary, join it to one exact native user entry, independently reopen
history, compare exact text/object serialization/identity and fsync through the
existing barrier. Then supervisor commits Accepted with the ordinary witness.
Preserve the old leaf/prefix and use existing linearEntries to prove an unchanged
linear continuation, allowing actual intervening assistant/tool/system entries
and already owning-witnessed user inputs. Reject unknown/crossed foreign users,
branch/context edits, changed prefix, duplicate/missing object and digest mismatch.
Update observePersisted AND verifyHistory consistently; never replace identity
with text/ordinal/queue-label matching. Multiple identical messages remain distinct.

Enqueue does not replace activeRef/Worker.activeInput. Keep original callbacks
valid while their tools finish. At actual consumption bind new active provenance;
new host calls wait for that input's native witness AND committed Accepted receipt.
Resolve calls against their exact operation from the bounded owned/accepted input
registry and existing native-origin proof, rather than overwriting one global ref
at enqueue. A delayed original-run finally cannot clear a newer active input or
pending record. Existing tool guards and pre-effect workflow ACK remain intact.
No deadlock may depend on receipt completion or session EX from the enqueuer.

**Uncertainty and lifetime.** Persisted prepared/dispatching still means Unknown
without exact live same-process ownership. Project Pending only when that registry
proves the same worker/operation still pending; do not invent a durable Pending
phase. Restart/crash never reconstructs or dispatches native queues from receipts.
Abort/hold must stop native execution, clear native queues through public clearQueue
inside the exclusively owned boundary, settle unconsumed slots Unknown/held, and
preserve already consumed Accepted witnesses. Clearing labels does not prove
NotSubmitted. EOF/dispose must settle all waiters; no hang waiting for a user event
that can no longer occur. Receipt commit failure holds/aborts; no later silent
consumption after unresolved state. Settings/apply-policy/unload/upgrade remain
blocked by active/pending/unknown work under existing semantics.

**Browser behavior.** Fresh current active status + supported capability shows
Steer now primary and Queue message secondary; idle primary is Send. Both use the
existing message path with explicit mode (primary steer; secondary followUp), same
text/files and one saved ID. Native decides the admitted idle race; UI status is
not mutation authority. Acknowledge Pending as a queued-item state, retire only
its local transport-FIFO barrier, retain the existing attempt with ID/mode/files.
Thus a later explicit steer can pass a native-queued followUp. Do not pass an
unresolved local Unknown head. Enqueued followUps/steers are not Sent until Accepted.
Reconcile exact Pending records through bounded existing refresh scheduling and
same-ID enquiry; reload never creates a new input or repeats enqueue. Unsupported
legacy worker capability leaves local drafts/FIFO unchanged and does not relabel
old attempts. Old terminal35af remains terminal; no conversion or resend. Preserve
terminal-proof marker and existing explicit replacement/Unknown safeguards.
No native queued-message deletion/edit API is introduced: browser Drop only applies
to not-yet-admitted local items, and cannot claim to cancel a Pending native input.

**Capability and delivery.** Publish `piInputDelivery:1` in the immutable runtime
contract; Manager reads the CURRENT runtime's frozen Start.AppStorePath, not the

After final C/R quick checks, committed affected review, packaged qualification

### Follow-up: reported Responses Lite parallel-tool refusal

User supplied a failed-turn message requiring `parallel_tool_calls=false` with
`X-OpenAI-Internal-Codex-Responses-Lite` after choosing Astra6.2. The session,
backend, provider and actual sending client are unspecified. This is separate
from the earlier catalog read and proves neither model entitlement nor route
identity. No unspecified session, failed input or credentials were inspected.

Source binding: the known installed Codex package `2rqwqchj...` assembles
`94pabrw...codex-0.165.0`; its source derivation pins `rust-v0.165.0` with source
NAR hash `sha256-b9PpwNQeZsJIN4wbGA3FLfWAKd2EDMN5E/zj/Y62/vk=`. The source output
is absent locally; inspected corresponding upstream tag tree
`360319d8dee62d87e2d59fc0c21805d79519cfed`, without realizing a derivation.
The package patch is daemon Nix-store handling, not request capability logic.

In that source, `codex-rs/core/src/client.rs:1118` serializes
`parallel_tool_calls: prompt.parallel_tool_calls && !model_info.use_responses_lite`.
Lines 2515–2521 add the Lite HTTP header only for that same metadata flag; the
HTTP and WebSocket builders pass the same model metadata. Recognized Lite
metadata therefore already forces false and also changes tools/reasoning shape.
The inspected TurnStartParams/ThreadStartParams schemas have no parallel-call
field. `core/config.schema.json` exposes no model/session toggle: its
`supports_parallel_tool_calls` field belongs to RawMcpServerConfig. The supported
`model_catalog_json` override applies at startup only; per-thread overrides are
explicitly no-ops. It is not an independent per-session request-flag repair.

`models-manager/src/model_info.rs:97–148` creates missing-model fallback metadata
with empty reasoning levels and `use_responses_lite=false`; manager.rs:989–998
selects it when no descriptor is found. Missing metadata can therefore omit
needed Lite formatting, but also omits Codex's own Lite header. It does not alone
establish the observed header/body mismatch. Gateway behavior, another client or
different effective metadata remain hypotheses, not diagnoses.

Official OpenAI function-calling documentation describes the public false
parameter but does not diagnose the internal Lite header:
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling#parallel-function-calling.
Smallest follow-up is first identify the affected session/backend, then inspect
only its retained model/provider/client-version and sanitized original failure
context under lead scope. No retry, provider trial, config/catalog rewrite,
transport patch, restart or dependency upgrade follows from present evidence.
Preserve defaults and saved choices; W zdr7 controls selection remains independent.
