### Memory requirement and existing lifecycle limit

Current eager Create starts one Node process per loaded member plus one Go
supervisor per session. Idle/closed tabs retain processes. This does not meet the
user's required aggregate parity with shared Codex, and no default Pi expansion
is justified. Existing ~97–118MiB samples are not a many-team comparison. Lead's
single host snapshot is 94.275GiB total, 51.420GiB available, no swap; it does not
make idle-per-member scaling acceptable.

Existing Unload/Load preserves IDs/history/settings/receipts and proves exit;
Unload refuses busy/held/unresolved inputs/settings/policy/callbacks/children.
Load admits only positively unloaded state; a crashed formerly loaded worker
stays held. But Bind/Read need snapshots and ObserveWorkflow refuses unloaded
members, while dispatch readiness needs that observation. A timer alone would
break read/send. Economical idle orchestration therefore needs retained read-only
metadata/history, explicit new-work wake of only the target member followed by
fresh admission, and guarded Unload together. GET/lookup/reconciliation must never
wake or replay; native Pending and Unknown cannot unload. This is not a format
migration but it is a consequential lifecycle package, NOT released here.
It can reduce idle cost only; active-worker aggregate parity remains unproven.
Use existing shared Codex as the bounded lighter baseline before promising Pi
parity. Do not replace worker isolation with a new multi-agent daemon or quietly
migrate current Pi sessions. No process was stopped or unloaded in this design.

### SDK support versus our bridge boundary

Installed1.5.2 `core/sdk.js:75,252,304` takes a supplied ModelRuntime and constructs
separate Agent and AgentSession objects per call. `sdk.d.ts:16` declares the public
injection. `AgentSession.dispose:1072` cleans that session's listeners/resources;
it does not dispose the shared ModelRuntime. Multiple sessions in one Node process
and one canonical runtime are therefore source-supported composition, not a need
for an SDK fork/upgrade. Independent SessionManager, settings, tools, extension
loader and callback/input ownership remain necessary. Sharing ModelRuntime is
safe only within identical canonical auth/catalog configuration: public extension
provider/virtual-model registration mutates that shared runtime, so arbitrary
session-local provider registration must not leak across members. Our current
fixed trusted configuration forbids such custom registrations.

The per-member processes were deliberate, not imposed by Pi. Our earlier
`process-isolation-evidence.md:9–40` records the user's requirement: “One session
cgroup/namespace, with team worker processes inside.” Design276/713 retained that
shape for separate event loops/failures and child ownership; design5590 already
said dormant members need no permanent workers. Current eager creation and no
idle unload do not realize that economical dormant-member intent.

Smallest plausible shared topology is ONE Node host within EACH existing session
supervisor/cgroup/namespace, with separate in-process AgentSessions/member stores
and at most one same-configuration ModelRuntime. No cross-session pool, migration
format, new scheduler or Pi Durable rewrite. Module/V8 baseline would be paid once
per team rather than member, but incremental histories/resources still cost RAM
and a process crash affects every loaded member. Savings remain unmeasured.

This is not a safe process-launch-only edit: current protocol owns one fixed
identity/session; worker PID/group exit proves per-member Unload and descendant
quiescence. A multiplexed host must keep every request/event/HostBridge/witness
bound to the original member/incarnation, isolate abort/queues/settings, mark all
unresolved inputs Unknown on host loss, and replace member-unload proof without
claiming that disposing an object proves process-group exit. The required
per-member process boundary and child-exit proof are the consequential decisions
for lead before implementation; retain them until an accepted substitute exists.

Proportional next step is a bounded topology feasibility unit on the pinned SDK:
source/prototype comparison of one versus representative six sessions within one
session boundary, same histories/tools, no provider input; verify independent
abort/dispose/events and no cross-member settings/receipt leakage, then one
controlled aggregate-PSS measurement if authorized. Compare separate ModelRuntime
versus safely shared runtime only if that distinction materially changes cost.
Do not start an alternatives project or idle-hibernation subsystem. U/P continue;
no native/worker/lifecycle implementation or experiment is authorized here.

### Detach, configure and retained compatibility

Ordinary reads/send and model/effort Configure remain member scoped. Configure
keeps that member's idle/noUnknown/noPending/callback/settings CAS guards and
must not mutate credential runtime/catalog. Do not require all siblings idle.

attribute native shell descendants to a member. Preserve its refusal when such
descendants exist, rather than accepting unknown effects or inventing a tool
process ledger. Sibling inference alone is not a refusal. Report this narrow
restriction explicitly; do not broaden it into a team-wide Save gate. Provider/
account rebinding or runtime mutation is outside this package.

Detach/upgrade uses a SHORT whole-host admission fence: every attached member
positively quiescent, no unresolved receipts/settings/policy/callbacks, then the
existing cgroup/registered-resource unknown-child check before and after member
disposal. New work cannot race this fence. If a sibling is busy, refuse detach;
never abort it. Same PID is deduplicated naturally. A disposal ACK is NOT OS exit.
Extend existing StopResult with optional VerifiedDetach; intermediate unload is
Outcome=detached, VerifiedDetach=true, VerifiedExit=false. Persist Loaded=false
only after positive disposal and postcheck. Repeat unload of a positively detached
member returns detach proof, never fabricates process exit. Last-member unload
closes the shared host, Waits and proves process-group/cgroup quiescence before
Outcome=stopped/VerifiedExit=true. Existing worker.Wait always means process exit.
Upgrade accepts intermediate detach only under the frozen new worker contract;
final predecessor terminal Host.Stop/drain receipt MUST prove physical host exit
before successor start. Registered resources retain their existing ownership.

Use the EXISTING protocol/metadata path: workerProtocol/manifest Protocol2 selects
multiplexing and detach semantics; keep the same strict schema1 envelope/framing.

assumes new semantics from the selected portal alone. Persist optional strict

legacy unique-process semantics. Existing schema1/2 otherwise stays unchanged.

as independently killable. Write it only for an actual shared attachment or its
positively detached retained record. Preserve creation/native/history/settings/
receipt identities and instruction/schema rules. No bulk rewrite on read.

workers with unchanged protocol1 VerifiedExit proof, then attaches retained
members to the new shared host. Existing ambiguity/Unknown blocks transition.
No automatic crashed-Loaded repair or restart/replay; use existing held recovery.
Rollback must use a compatible reader and the same proven drain/successor path;
an old binary reading shared records fails closed. Do not erase the topology
marker or rewrite receipts to make downgrade appear supported.

member settings/access/instructions. Remove the Pi tab's assignment composer;

accepted the removal version fence and supported-consumer scope below; allocation
and the application/index window follow the rules owner's terminal handoff.

four-column presentations; Add already shares the same controls. pi_teams.go576+
refuses DELETE and supports only Add/assign. PiRoster.Validate accepts removed
metadata but SavePi190+ forbids ready-to-nonready/RemovedAt changes. Native
conversation.go1029+ already provides positive shared VerifiedDetach or final
VerifiedExit, preserving history/receipts/settings. No new native RPC is needed.
The shared host's existing quiescence/descendant fence is a real removal constraint:
busy/held/uncertain target or sibling can prevent removal; show the precise reason
through the common action, never abort a sibling or weaken that fence.

**Portal interface/UI.** Use the existing member-status/table/Add/settings/action

thread creation; expose state through the same row, not another UI.

settings use the existing conversation settings/catalog interface with that row's
admitted conversation scope and frozen generation, never the selected page's or
Codex root identity. Fetch current allowed choices through the owning adapter;

with a reason and retain ordinary conversation navigation where supported. No

EX; recheck exact session/generation, root scope, pending lifecycle/provider state,

## Fork choices parity — sufficient implementation brief (2026-11-19)

**Settled scope and release boundary.** The user's explicit two-mode answer
supersedes selected-nonlead-to-new-lead proposals and the earlier new-Fork
no-settings/no-team non-goal. Old accepted operations keep their original meaning.
This brief is sufficient for one implementation package after the Team owner
releases overlapping R source/index files. Team remains independently accepted;
architect0 owns this design only. Recommend implementer2 after Team, with lead
allocation and main's final visible wording. No application edits, checks or live
Fork are performed by this brief.

**One portal interface.** Extend the existing session Fork route with root-scoped
choices and submission through its Codex/Pi adapters. One dialog, provider/model/
effort controls, team picker, progress and retry interaction consume the same
view/request. Choices contain current root scope, supported copy modes, Keep current
team plus installed presets, exact role capacities, lead settings/catalog choices,
provider scope and explicit unavailable reasons. The options read does not Load,
Configure or capture history. Submission revalidates all selections under ordinary
admission before reservation. A viewed member never supplies the history source;
new operations always use root/team scope and open the destination lead. Do not
weaken selected-member scope checks or use Codex IDs for Pi. Retained legacy member
selection applies only to the original accepted operation's recovery/navigation.

Default is Copy the team + Keep current team + inherit lead settings. The modes:

- **Copy the team:** preserve every nonremoved source address, exact role and saved
  policy/settings; copy every materialized conversation. Include genuine unstarted
  reservations in required capacity without inventing history. Keep removed metadata
  and retired addresses, with no native copy. For a selected preset, each source role
  count must fit that exact target role's count; equal total size is insufficient.
  Reject missing roles or smaller capacity before destination reservation. Retain
  source order/addresses; consume that many target slots per role in preset order.
  Append remaining target slots in preset order with normal next-unused indices over
  all retained addresses/tombstones. No renaming, role substitution or heuristic map.
- **Copy only the lead:** copy the source root history and its policy, regardless of
  viewed member. All teammates are fresh from the selected installed preset; smaller
  teams and Solo are allowed. Keep current team here means the saved role layout and
  saved role defaults as fresh slots, with no teammate origins/history/receipts; retain
  its retired address reservations so a removed address is not silently reused. An
  explicitly selected different preset starts its own fresh address space. Source
  tombstones/history remain untouched. No unrelated conversation is promoted.

Copied role/access/instructions/provider/model/effort/tool ceiling remain saved;
target preset defaults apply only to fresh slots. Explicit lead settings override
only destination settings. Freeze both original source provenance and selected
installed preset/catalog snapshot: a composed team digest cannot pretend the mixed
roster is an unchanged installed preset. Reuse the existing direct-team snapshot
and per-member policy fields, with the composition/provenance in the accepted Fork
record. Fresh slots have genuine destination identities and creation timestamps;
no source incarnation, fork origin, native ID or input receipt is fabricated. Pi
leaves them unstarted until real assignment. Codex may perform its established empty
native initialization; neither adapter sends a user assignment/model turn to make a
fresh member look copied. Partial creation is not a true unstarted reservation.

**Settings and genuine constraints.** Inherit freezes observed source settings,
including source provider, rather than following a later workspace default. Validate
inherited initialization and final selected pairs against the destination package's
actual configured accounts/routes/catalog and tool/instruction support before any
reservation. Do not infer support from a descriptor alone or require live model
completions. Model changes refresh effort choices and preserve a still-valid effort;
otherwise require a valid explicit choice, never silently lower xhigh or change
saved source settings. Access/instructions remain inherited for copied members;
there is no new access-grant selector.

Codex's provider is session-scoped (workspacecodex/client.go providerSettings,
state.Provider(slug, root); dev-session prepare_provider_selection!/bind-root).
With any retained active nonlead, including true unstarted reservations, Copy the
team must pin source provider and reject a different value before effects. Copy
only the lead, or Copy the team from an actual Solo, permits an available destination
provider; fresh Codex members use that provider. Model/effort remain lead-specific.
Expose provider scope through the adapter in the same control, disabled with source
value only when this restriction applies. Main supplied this exact help text:
“This backend uses one provider for the whole session. To change it, choose Copy

## Held callback recovery feasibility — disposition, not implementation release (2026-11-19)

**Scope and outcome.** This bounded read-only package does not amend the accepted
recurrence correction above. No current public operation can reconcile an existing
`forwarded callback outcome unknown` hold. The safe retained-state findings are in
[tmp/pi-usability/team-ui-parity/recovery-feasibility.json](tmp/pi-usability/team-ui-parity/recovery-feasibility.json),
verified ignored and untracked. They distinguish delivery evidence from full caller
and shared-host settlement. No target mutation, native call, test or build occurred.
There is no sufficient restoration implementation package to release on this evidence.

**Available proof and its limit.** The input owner writes a durable intent before
enqueue; its exact original input/receipt and native history can establish whether
that input was submitted. An empty member's saved native mapping is a real creation
effect, even while the public binding and roster remain creating without a published
native ID. Recovery must preserve that incarnation, creation ID, original first-input
reservation, settings, instructions and history reference. Matching disk records are
not a substitute for the existing positive VerifyCreation/native settings proof.
Every caller's accepted input witness and every unresolved host invocation must be
covered; resolving one missing recipient input does not settle sibling callbacks.
Matched tool-result entries and a cgroup sample with no child command are useful
observations, but neither proves that all in-memory or external effects have settled.

**Exact source boundaries.** At deployed 8fe50341, piruntime/callback_types.go and
callbacks.go authenticate the original input, native tool, anchor, linear selection,
arguments digest and runtime/member subject before forwarding. The attachment's
pending map is ephemeral; no durable authenticated callback/result ledger exists.
InspectNativeOrigin (conversation.go610) can reread a loaded held caller's saved
invocation, but explicitly grants no callback authority and does not repeat its
original Accepted-input proof. A digest reconstructed from history is not a saved
HostCall. Any future reconciliation must positively bind both proofs to the same
original invocation and account for every retained unknown callback.

ObserveWorkflow (workflow_observation.go199) is ephemeral display proof. It combines
held state into Idle=false and does not export all native activity counters; it cannot
certify otherwise-settled held work. The existing hostAdmission.detach fence is
internal. sharedQuiescentLocked and JS assertForkQuiescent reject holds. There is no
public fenced held-settlement observation or exact callback reconciliation operation.
VerifyCreation, Lookup and historical-origin reads cannot clear the Go callbackUnknown,
durable HeldReason and native JS held state. ReconcilePiMessage belongs to saved
cross-session communication receipts; it cannot be repurposed for team callback holds.

**Old-runtime delivery barrier.** supervisor.invoke has no reconciliation dispatch,
and session.mjs has no unhold operation. The owning Go supervisor and JS worker are
frozen with their launch package. A newly selected portal cannot retrofit either.
Normal runtime upgrade requires assertRuntimeSettledExcept (successor_proof.go93)
and positive predecessor drain; it refuses these holds. Unload, Fork, retrying creation,
input replay or a restart do not establish recovery authority. Do not remove holds
from records, relax successor admission, replace a member, or treat process exit as
proof of the original effects. The recurrence correction can ship independently;
it does not restore this predecessor.

**Decision and minimal next options.** Keep the retained session and evidence intact
while delivering prevention. If restoration of this exact session is required, lead
must separately decide a legacy-compatible recovery boundary before implementation.
That decision must address both missing evidence and how the old supervisor can
participate; adding an RPC only to a new package is not a solution for this predecessor.
The minimum eventual contract would bind the original authenticated callback/input/
native-tool/argument tuple, exact recipient reservation and positively verified native
creation/settings, exact no-enqueue or immutable original delivery proof, all other
callback/input/resource obligations, and current host/process ownership under exclusion.
It would preserve original failed tool results and all history, never resend, and
retain the hold on any unknown or mismatched proof. No generic clear API or replacement
journal is proposed here. A concrete legacy delivery path and complete settlement
proof remain blockers, not implementation details left to the recurrence owner.

Existing read ports could narrow historical/native proof gaps in a separately scoped
read, and a privileged read could establish the host receipt tuple where access is
missing. Neither would create the absent recovery operation or justify clearing a
hold. No additional read campaign is needed to establish this capability gap. Any
future accepted recovery package needs focused disposable controls for exact success,
wrong origin/input/digest/incarnation, concurrent sibling effects, partial creation,
lost reconciliation response and old-package delivery; no live target trial is implied.

## Shared subscription authentication — recovery proposal only (2026-11-19)

**Disposition.** The retained native auth manager classifies refresh failure as a
revoked refresh token. The affected discovery error and those auth failures share
the same native process identity. This is positive authentication-failure evidence;
last_refresh age alone was not used to infer expiry. Repeated native error entries
can reflect a cached permanent rejection and are not a count of HTTP refresh calls.
Revocation actor/reason, the original upstream body and a complete successful-refresh
history remain unknown. Safe metadata and the unchanged original report are linked
from [tmp/pi-usability/team-ui-parity/routing-401/auth-diagnosis.json](tmp/pi-usability/team-ui-parity/routing-401/auth-diagnosis.json).
No new account HTTP, native discovery, login, refresh or execution probe was made.
The user subsequently reported no recent authentication changes. That observation
does not identify who or what revoked the credential; the cause of revocation remains
unknown.

**Owning boundary.** The running assembled native0.165.0 uses the registered
workspace Codex home, shared by its subscription sessions. Allowlisted process/config
metadata found no API/access-token override, bootstrap/refresh URL override or local
forced-account setting. The selected custom-provider default does not replace a saved
subscription session's provider. Package assembly materializes upstream resources;
it does not patch Rust authentication. The pending Team/messaging/limits work is not
deployed and does not supply a causal native auth change. No application/native source
fix is warranted by current evidence, and the portal provider-alias404 remains separate.

**Evidence limits.** The reference native source5b0cea5e fits the observed diagnostic:
login/src/auth/manager.rs classifies invalidated refresh credentials as revoked, and
workspace-routing discovery retries through guarded reload/refresh. Its successful
same-account reload replaces cached auth; a changed account is refused. Relevant
messages and device-login support are present in the deployed ELF. The realized
native derivation source remains unavailable locally, so these reference anchors
are not a complete source-to-final-byte certificate. No fetch/build expansion is
needed to identify the supported account recovery path. Token claims and JWT expiry
were not inspected because the explicit failure classification already resolves that
question. No credential values, headers or raw logs were output or retained.

**Concrete proposed operation, for main/user decision.** After authorization for
shared authentication renewal, the user/operator can run the installed native login
against the same workspace home:

```sh
env CODEX_HOME=/home/aither/.local/state/dev-workspaces/codex-homes/vpsfree-cz \
  /nix/store/2rqwqchjlv6l2nw5l491pkhvrsijn50c-codex-package-0.165.0/bin/codex \
  login --device-auth
```

This command is a proposal and was not run. The user must complete its browser/device
flow with the same ChatGPT account and workspace. Device-code login must be enabled
for that account/workspace. Do not substitute an API key, switch provider, copy another
home's auth file, or invoke login without the explicit workspace home. The official
[Codex authentication guide](https://developers.openai.com/codex/auth/) documents
interactive login, device-code prerequisites and shared file/keyring storage. The
installed entrypoint is a wrapper around the same native ELF; no portal login endpoint
or new recovery framework is needed. If device login is unavailable, ordinary browser
login with the documented SSH callback forwarding is an operator alternative to plan
separately, preserving this home and normal temporary-server ownership.

**Effects and recovery boundary.** Login changes the shared subscription credential
store; the reference login owner clears/revokes old auth before completing sign-in.
Treat cancellation/failure as possibly leaving subscription authentication unavailable.
This affects all subscription sessions using that home. It is not a session/provider
switch, does not replace conversations/history/settings/rosters, and does not justify
a service restart. Existing native managed-auth recovery can adopt changed credentials
for the same account. Preserve account identity using nonsecret metadata; a successful
login to a different account is not equivalent recovery. No standalone logout or manual
auth-file edit is part of this proposal.

**Existing App Server cache adoption.** The supported path does not require a
restart. In the reference auth owner, the next managed auth read needing proactive
refresh first performs a same-account guarded reload (`manager.rs:2603`, `3349`).
Changed persisted credentials replace the cached credentials without another refresh
exchange; publication clears the old credential's permanent-refresh failure and
advances auth generation (`manager.rs:3037-3100`). The routing discovery owner also
starts unauthorized recovery with this reload (`workspace_routing.rs:403-451`).
Thus a completed login to the same account/workspace can be adopted by the running
App Server on its next applicable auth read/recovery. This is demand-driven adoption,
not proof of an immediate file-watcher update, and it does not replay failed work.
A different account is refused by guarded recovery. The deployed-byte/source limit
above still applies; actual adoption is an acceptance observation after authorized
login, not something demonstrated by this read-only investigation.

**Acceptance and ownership.** Main owns authorization and execution coordination;
the user owns interactive authentication. First require native login success and the
intended same account/workspace. Login success proves stored authentication, not that
every failed operation has resumed. A separately authorized existing subscription read
or normal continuation must establish native acceptance; preserve its actual scope and
report any remaining401. Do not automatically replay failed turns or team assignments,
create replacement IDs, clear holds, restart a service, or bypass receipt/recovery

### Acceptance status and composer separation — sufficient UI amendment (2026-11-19)

**Lead disposition supersedes receipt-blocked composer behavior.** A proposal
awaiting consent, a captured acceptance and ordinary conversation readiness are
three different states. Captured/pending/held acceptance must not indefinitely
hide conversation controls. Keep retained proposal content and original request
status visible; restore the ordinary composer/steer UI through its existing
readiness, scope, worker hold, ordering, loading and inflight guards. Rendering a
receipt never grants Send/Steer permission or changes dispatch. Main owns final
visible copy. Owner1 may implement this bounded projection in its isolated source
window; original R42 delivery remains independent.

found the sole original acceptance held in both full snapshot and exact status,

state lag. Sanitized exact identities/status and the honest first-parser failure

7e59b908483440e91d978dc86dea9e34c90effa7f9b58b682b605e830717db73).
All reads joined. Domain held is distinct from worker held. Public phase cannot
distinguish NotSubmitted from Unknown: `piplan.Service.Advance` maps non-Accepted
Lookup results and unsuccessful/uncertain checked Send to held. No success,
ongoing execution or cancellation may be inferred from generic Saved.

**Minimal phase/visibility contract.** Apply this with the already accepted shared
retained proposal list, not a new modal, history owner or receipt schema:

| Existing evidence | Proposal/status presentation | Decision controls and composer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Latest proposal, no acceptance and no local attempted request | Exact readable proposal; ordinary consent question | Existing Implement eligibility and Keep planning; decision may hide composer as before. |
| Original browser request persisted, capture POST still inflight | Saving request; no delivery claim | No second approval; retain existing short inflight control/focus guards. |
| POST settled but outcome unconfirmed, original local pending survives | Request outcome unconfirmed; original Check request | No new approval/ID for that proposal; stop treating this as unanswered consent. Restore ordinary composer eligibility. |
| Server phase prepared | Saved; waiting to start implementation | Hide consent controls; original Check request remains; ordinary composer eligibility restored. Do not claim a particular busy cause. |
| Server phase mode_pending | Implementation preparation not yet confirmed | Same restored ordinary composer; original Check request. Do not retry policy. |
| Server phase dispatch_pending | Implementation delivery not yet confirmed | Same; do not claim input Accepted or resend. |
| Server phase held | Implementation request on hold; delivery not confirmed by this public view | Same; original Check request. Do not label it actively running, automatically retrying or still awaiting consent. |
| Server phase accepted | Implementation request accepted (not task completion) | No approval or resend; accepted status/body retained; ordinary composer eligibility restored. |
| Read failure/unknown phase/stale scope | Retain known scoped bodies/status with unavailable/unconfirmed feedback; never upgrade outcome | Disable unproved plan actions. Preserve ordinary operation's own guards; scope replacement tears down foreign DOM and prevents late reads from restoring it. |

"pi-delivery-v1:steer", Retry:false}, settings)`. Ref binds the recipient's full
conversation, original message ID and Action=send. The message's immutable

Envelope construction separates quoted peer text from a bounded runtime-generated
authorization snapshot of the typed grant/endpoints/message/audit/scope. It tells
the recipient that an active pair is bidirectional and that later replies still

same-process enqueue returned it. A persisted submitting record is not proof of

Exactly one must equal the saved Digest; zero or multiple matches refuse/hold.
Then lookup ONLY that original ref and require complete equality of Schema1,

ID, nonempty witness entry and exact envelope digest; NotSubmitted needs its
explicit refusal. Pending/Unknown remain nonterminal and cannot become accepted
by inference. Preserve existing nonnil terminal outcomes/transition rules and
CAS the original message after releasing the read gate before the later write.

## Automatic continuation of submitted browser intent — sufficient bounded brief (2026-11-20)

fresh read if Pi readiness is absent. `restartConversationSync:7799-7844` drains

attribution and total send latency are not prerequisites or conclusions.

wake and successful sync apply only. Extend existing

current runners suffice. Correct the existing waiting/reload paragraphs in

stream_incomplete work is independent. No relabel-only substitute.

**Settled state contract.** Remove restoration as a reason to pause. Reconcile
saved FIFO entries with existing exact scoped send/queue attempt records before
any automatic drain or receipt projection can overwrite their meaning. Eligible
ordinary intent is the FIFO head in `waiting`, with no prior-retry indicator,
matching original ID/text/action/context/delivery/attachment order, and no drop,
replacement-recovery, terminal failure, pending-native or accepted contradiction.
`retry:false` (or a supported legacy absent false default) is not Unknown recovery.
Missing/corrupt storage, mismatched payload or ambiguous copy remains blocked.
Do not invent replacement identities or reconstruct missing records to proceed.

The FIFO is the existing before-HTTP boundary: `drain:354` durably writes and
verifies `unknown` BEFORE `send:6934-6942` stores the attempt and invokes HTTP.
A valid producer-written waiting entry can therefore continue with its original
ID. Important compatibility detail: `sendAttemptStore:1184-1220` omits both initial
and Unknown states; `loadMessageReceipts:5155` presents either as Unknown by default.
That absent receipt state ALONE must not veto a matching never-dispatched FIFO,
nor certify an isolated receipt as unsent. Queue receipts likewise omit phase.
Recognized saved drop/copy/failed/Pending/accepted/observed facts take precedence.
Do not mark restored entries in the in-memory `fresh` set: existing exact
validation-error classification still needs its original first-dispatch proof.
The synthetic restored retry:false refusal control at handoff-test:356-361 must
still end Unknown after its ambiguous refusal, not acquire fresh failure proof.

After initialization and after acceptance/original witness, safe drop or resolved
predecessor, recompute the head's eligibility; do not carry an unrelated global
restore pause into the safe tail. Keep one active request, FIFO order and the
verified Unknown write before HTTP. Explicit Drop, failure editing/copy decisions,

preserve the blanket internal pause. Native Queue next/followUp remains its saved

after capture when it cannot yet dispatch, and consider eligible heads after a
successful CURRENT sync apply for both adapters and normal readiness restoration.
Do not dispatch while initialization/receipt reconciliation is incomplete, hidden,

session/member/native identity, scope/incarnation and revision/generation checks;

status becoming green or SSE reconnect alone is not readiness. Repeated applies,

backs off failures, coalesces hints and recovers on online/focus/visibility. Reuse

A session hold, authorization/scope refusal, terminal validation, invalid storage
or unresolved outcome stops mutation until its actual condition is resolved.
No automatic authentication/authority repair, shorter poll or arbitrary deadline.
Navigating back/reloading the same retained tab can resume eligible intent; a
closed tab has no executing dispatcher and this change promises no server outbox.

Unknown stays on the original ID and remains an ordering barrier until exact
receipt/transcript proof resolves it. Retain existing Pi delivery lookup-only and

waiting entry into a fresh send or introduce generic automatic Unknown retry.

## 2026-11-21 ready Pi temporary services: sufficient independent B brief

Status: source diagnosis complete; ready for lead allocation to implementer1.
Baseline is literal R23df140729484774862b3ce5f9f0bacdc2bc1cbb/tree6fbe73d3,
selected mimnv52 package; current C3209 and deployed host remain unchanged.

No implementation, checks, service launch/stop or peer mutation were performed.

**Cause and boundary.** `libexec/workspace-session-services.rb:275–298` routes
run/stop through `with_creation_lock`, `with_slug_lock`, and
`require_ordinary_manifest_ready!`. Both lock helpers enforce Codex before and
after lock acquisition (`libexec/dev-session:9039–9080`); the first refusal is
therefore in the creation lock, before the session lock or service Store. The
legacy backend guard refuses schema4/5 (`workspace-session-backends.rb:126`),
and the ordinary manifest validator independently accepts only schema1/3.
The reported error is explained by this wiring, not a missing Pi validator or
MariaDB/nodectld failure. The supplied ephemeral stderr/service-id paths were
already absent at this read; the peer's launch/no-effects statements remain
reported evidence rather than independently re-established effects.

**Chosen correction.** Reuse the existing strict ready-Pi local mutation path
